chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: I fast, so I do not take a midday rest when the sun declines. Then when the sun declines, I perform my nawāfil, then I perform the ẓuhr, then I perform my nawāfil, then I perform the ʿaṣr, then I sleep, and that is before the people pray. So he said: O Zurārah, when the sun declines, the time has entered; but I dislike for you to make it a fixed constant time. Then if it is said: You have mentioned that when the sun declines, the time of the obligatory prayer has entered, then you said that beginning with the nawāfil is better, and this conflicts with what has been narrated in the reports that there is no supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الْوَقْتُ: the legally recognized time for prayer
key_terms.تَزُولُ: declines from the zenith, marking the entry of the prayer time
key_terms.لَا تَطَوُّعَ: no supererogatory prayer is to be performed in that legal circumstance
key_terms.نَوَافِلِي: my supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory prayers

ai.seo_question: When does the time of ẓuhr begin, and can nawāfil be performed after the sun declines?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the beginning of the time for ẓuhr prayer and the relationship between obligatory and supererogatory prayers at that time. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the prayer time begins at the sun’s decline, while indicating dislike for treating that exact moment as a rigid constant personal habit, and the report raises the legal question of performing nawāfil when the time of an obligatory prayer has already entered.
